## Triage routing

**Labels** `tooling` `finding` `domain:devx` `pm:queue` `priority:p3` · **Type** Task

**Lane — `domain:devx`.** The gate is `scripts/check-vi-mock-inherit.mjs` and the fix lands in `scripts/__tests__/check-vi-mock-inherit.test.ts` — the engineering face, and the gate's subject is test-mock hygiene rather than any product contract.

**Re-measured on `83d4fda16` — the card's central claim holds, and I verified it the way it needs verifying: by looking for the pin that would refute it.**

The one membership assertion is at **`:1185`** — `).toContain(I18N);`. Searching the whole test file for any equivalent pin on `@object-ui/react` finds **none**: the only occurrences are `:25` (a prose docblock), `:61` (`const COVERED = '@object-ui/react'` — a **fixture constant**, not an assertion about the real list), `:563` (a prefix-boundary case), and `:1090` (a comment). ⛔ `:61` is the one a hasty reader would mistake for a pin; it is not one.

The generic assertions are at `:469-479` and are exactly as the card's table describes:
```ts
expect(COVERED_SPECIFIERS.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
for (const spec of COVERED_SPECIFIERS) { … expect(…name).toBe(spec); }
```
⭐ And that test's **own comment** states the limit the card is pointing at: *"A typo here empties the population silently, and the gate then reports OK over nothing."* — i.e. it was written against **emptying**, not against **removing one member**. The card is not disagreeing with the guard; it is observing that the guard's stated scope and the ratchet's stated promise are not the same size.

**Admission — class (b), violation of a declared contract.** `check-vi-mock-inherit.mjs`'s header states the covered set is **GROW-ONLY**, and the ratchet's entire force rests on that. The enforcement covers one member.

**The mechanism, restated because it is the part that must survive into the fix:** `findCallSites` classifies a call site as `covered` only when its specifier is in `COVERED_SPECIFIERS`; everything else is `workspace` / `unjudged`. So **removing** a member reddens nothing — it makes that specifier's whole population invisible and the gate reports OK over a tree it no longer looks at. Deleting `@object-ui/react` leaves `check:vi-mock-inherit` green, the guard's own suite green (`length > 0` still holds, i18n still present), and **134 sites unwatched**. The three specifiers objectui#6892 slice 1 adds inherit the same gap.

**⛔ The obvious backstop does not reach, and the card measured why.** `FLOORS.covered = 50` (`check-vi-mock-inherit.mjs:1186`) is the nearest thing: with `@object-ui/react` removed the covered count is still **95** (i18n's 92 plus the three 1-site specifiers) — comfortably above the floor. It only catches a collapse to *near-nothing*, which is the case it was written for. ⛔ Do not "fix" this by raising the floor: a floor is a count, and the defect is about *which* population is being counted.

**Grade p3.** Nothing is wrong today — no member has ever been removed and the gate is green. This is a guard-strength finding, filed because *the protection currently reads as general and is not*. Re-grade to p2 if a member is ever removed in a PR (which is the event the pin exists to catch, and would prove it does not).

**On the suggested shape — I endorse it and add one constraint.** Replacing the single-member `toContain(I18N)` with a pin over the **swept set** — every specifier a landed sweep has added, listed once, asserted present — keeps the existing case's rationale and makes it hold for all of them. The card's justification for why this is a ledger rather than an exemption table is correct: *each entry is justified by a merged sweep PR*.

⛔ The constraint: the new pin must be a **literal list**, not derived from `COVERED_SPECIFIERS` itself. The verdict-line case at `:977` (`const named = COVERED_SPECIFIERS.join(', ')`) is the cautionary example already in the file — it **adapts** to any removal rather than resisting it, which is precisely the property that makes it useless as a ratchet. A pin that reads its expectation from the thing it is pinning cannot fail. That is this repo's recurring shape and it is worth naming in the new test's docblock.

**Verified: nothing else reads the constant.** `git grep -l COVERED_SPECIFIERS` returns the gate, its test, **six** changesets and one workflow (`.github/workflows/vi-mock-specifiers.yml`) — no other consumer. The card said "one changeset"; there are six now, all inert for this purpose. So the pin really is the only protection there is.

**Correctly not fixed under objectui#6892 slice 1** — that slice's file surface is the three converted test files plus the three lines in the constant, and generalising this pin is a decision about the ratchet's own pin rather than part of the sweep.

Triage seat only — no claim, no dispatch, no code.

### Adjudication section

⛔ **No maintainer ruling applies.** The constraints are the card's and triage's (`5583428563`).

### ⚠️ The trap, carried in as a required discrimination

> ⛔ `:61` is the one a hasty reader would mistake for a pin; it is not one.

`check-vi-mock-inherit.test.ts:61` is `const COVERED = '@object-ui/react'` — a **fixture constant**, ⛔ not an assertion about the real list; the other occurrences are a docblock (`:25`), a prefix-boundary case (`:563`) and a comment (`:1090`). ⇒ **a symbol grep concludes "already pinned" and is wrong.** The dev must state how it established each occurrence's **syntactic role**, ⛔ not that it grepped.

⭐ And the guard's own comment names the gap exactly: *"A typo here empties the population silently, and the gate then reports OK over nothing."* — written against **emptying**, ⛔ not against **removing one member**. ⇒ the card is not disagreeing with the guard; the guard's stated scope and the ratchet's stated promise are not the same size.

### The change, and what it may not become

Dropping **any** member must redden, not just `@object-ui/i18n`. Shape decided before implementation and justified in the PR body, under these:

- ⛔ It must resist removal of **every** current member, including ones added later — ⚠️ a pin listing today's members by hand is itself a hand-copy that will drift, which is this repo's recurring disease.
- ⛔ It must not restate `COVERED_SPECIFIERS` from the same import: that asserts `x === x` and holds nothing. ⭐ **If the pin cannot fail, it is not a pin** — the mutation test is what proves it can.
- ⛔ Nothing existing is weakened: the `length > 0` floor, the real-package loop and `toContain(I18N)` all stay. ⛔ No threshold lowered, no assertion deleted, no test skipped.

### ⭐ The mutation test is the deliverable that proves the work

One leg per member, mutating the **gate** and ⛔ never the test; each mutation proven to have reached disk by **anchored grep or blob hash**, ⛔ not by an editor's exit code; restored under an `EXIT INT TERM` trap and proven restored by **blob hash**. ⭐ The load-bearing reading is that **exactly** the new pin fails and the rest of the suite keeps passing — plus a **control leg**: the same removal against the **unmodified** test file must leave it **green**, which is the defect reproduced. ⛔ Without that leg nothing has been shown to close.

`merged_at 2026-09-08T18:55:32Z`; `removed_from_merge_queue@18:55:31Z` with `merged: true` ⇒ that removal **is** the merge, ⛔ not a dequeue.

### ⚠️ First, this seat's own probe was wrong, and the wrong reading is published rather than dropped

The landing probe's ledger count came back **0** against a firing control of **21** on the gate side. ⛔ That was not a finding — it was **this seat's bad anchor**: the probe assumed a two-space indent, and `SWEPT_MEMBERS` lives inside a `describe`, indented **four**.

⭐ The errata this seat maintains already names that trap — *"an **anchored** pattern cannot answer a question about an indented region"* — and it walked into it anyway. ⇒ ⛔ **a zero from a pattern whose shape has not been controlled is not a reading**, and the correct response was to look at the text before reporting a defect, which is what happened.

### Landing probe, re-run correctly on a re-fetched `origin/main` (tip `1ebaf7217`)

| check | reading |
|:--|:--|
| the pin's parts | `SWEPT_MEMBERS` present; `NOTHING LEAVES the covered set …` × 1; `NOTHING JOINS unrecorded …` × 1 |
| ledger entries | **21** (`:523-543`) |
| ⭐ **firing control** — the gate's own `COVERED_SPECIFIERS` | **21** |

| in-class control | `@object-ui/react` found in **both** |
| negative control | `@object-ui/no-such-8018` found in **neither** — ⇒ the membership test can say no |

⚠️ Counting only the ledger side would have passed while the two silently diverged — **this card's own defect in miniature**, which is why the gate side is the firing control rather than an afterthought.

### What is now true that was not

The gate's header declares `COVERED_SPECIFIERS` **GROW-ONLY**, and its whole force rests on that: `findCallSites` marks a site `covered` only on membership, so **removing** a member reddens nothing — it makes that specifier's population invisible and the gate reports OK over a tree it no longer looks at. ⇒ from `1ebaf7217` a removal fails `NOTHING LEAVES`, and an **addition** that skips the ledger fails `NOTHING JOINS unrecorded` — so a member added later arrives already pinned, by the same PR that sweeps it.

⭐ **And the card understated its own defect.** Measured this round: the genuinely unprotected population was **18 of 21 members**, ⛔ not one — with the control leg proving it (removing any of those 18 against the unmodified test file left `86 passed (86)`, exit 0). ⚠️ `@object-ui/react` did redden 11 cases, but by **coincidence**: the fixture constant at `:61` happens to name a real member, so those cases fell out of `covered` — protection that depends on a fixture spelling and on which files exist, whose failure text names no ratchet. ⇒ the card's defect was real and **larger** than filed; its chosen exhibit was not.

⛔ `FLOORS.covered = 50` never backstopped it: the judged total is 666 and the largest single member is 136, so no single removal can push the total under the floor.

### The limit this keeps, stated rather than papered over

An author who deletes a member from the constant **and** its ledger line in one edit still passes. ⭐ That is the floor of any literal pin, and it is the intent: a member cannot leave **silently** — ⛔ not that it can never leave.
